title: Crisis familiares, relaciones y funcionamiento familiar en contextos vulnerables de una ciudad del caribe colombiano
abstract: This study examined the relationship between family crises, intrafamilial relationships, and family functioning (FF) in households from vulnerable neighborhoods in Cartagena, Colombia. A quantitative, cross-sectional, and correlational design was applied to a sample of 205 families. Most households face moderate poverty, overcrowding, environmental risks, and high rates of adolescent pregnancy and relational conflict. The findings show that both normative crises (life-cycle transitions) and non-normative crises (unexpected events like illness or loss) negatively affect family dynamics. Functional family systems—defined by open communication, emotional cohesion, and adaptability—are associated with greater emotional stability and psychological well-being, particularly in children and adolescents. The study concludes that strengthening family relationships can significantly enhance resilience in the face of adversity. It recommends public policies and community interventions that reinforce emotional bonds and promote adaptive coping strategies in vulnerable contexts.
